Refit a factorised model as a single joint fit

Source: R/bnec_joint.R
bnec_joint.Rd

Takes what a factorised fit favoured and refits it as one model expressing structure the factorisation could not. For a bayesnechurdlefit that is the model combination crossed_weights favours, refitted with a two-block (hurdle_gamma, zero_inflated_beta, hurdle_poisson or hurdle_negbinomial) family. For a bayesnecgroupfit it is the equation each level favours, composed into one model in which every curve parameter takes a separate value per level of the grouping factor, estimated in a single posterior.

bnec_joint(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
bnec_joint(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnechurdlefit'
bnec_joint(object, model = NULL, model_survival = NULL, formula = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnecgroupfit'
bnec_joint(object, model = NULL, formula = NULL, disp_by_level = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class bayesnechurdlefit returned by bnec_hurdle, or of class bayesnecgroupfit returned by bnec_group.

...

Further arguments passed to brm.

model

An optional character string naming the equation to fit. For a hurdle fit it is the response block's equation and defaults to the highest-weighted growth model in object. For a grouped fit it forces one equation at every level; the default is instead the equation each level's own weights favour, which may differ between levels.

model_survival

An optional character string naming the equation for the survival block. Defaults to the highest-weighted survival model in object. Hurdle fits only.

formula

An optional bayesnecformula to fit instead of the one held in object. Supply this to add structure the factorised fit cannot carry, for example a group-level term. The crf model argument is overwritten by model either way.

disp_by_level

A logical. Should the family's dispersion parameter also take a separate value per level? Defaults to TRUE. Grouped fits only.

Value

For a bayesnechurdlefit, an object of class bayesnecfit; for a bayesnecgroupfit, an object of class bayesnecjointfit.

Details

Why refit at all

The factorised and joint routes give equivalent inference where the two components are independent, so a joint refit of the same pair of equations adds nothing on its own – the estimates differ only by Monte Carlo noise. What it adds is the ability to write structure that spans the two blocks, which the factorisation cannot express by construction: a group-level effect shared between response and survival makes the two posteriors dependent, and a dependent posterior cannot be assembled from two fits run separately.

The division of labour is therefore: fit the model sets with bnec_hurdle, where all n_growth * n_survival combinations can be compared from two fits; choose a combination from crossed_weights; then refit that one jointly here, adding the shared structure. Model averaging happens in the first step, because the joint route can only average over the response block.

What is carried over

The response variable, predictor and data are taken from object, and the family follows the growth component: hurdle_gamma where that was fitted as a Gamma, zero_inflated_beta where it was a Beta, and the corresponding count hurdle where it was Poisson or negative binomial. Nothing else transfers – priors, control arguments and the like are defaults again unless passed through ....

A disp() term in the formula held in object is kept, and in the joint model it applies to the dispersion parameter of the positive block. The variance function is written in that block's mean and centred on the positive responses, as it is for the growth component, so the joint model fits the same variance function (see bnec). A formula supplied here replaces the held one, so a disp() term is fitted only where it is written in that formula. hurdle_negbinomial does not yet take a disp() term, so a negative binomial growth component fitted with one is refused before anything is fitted; supply a formula without the term to refit it jointly with one shape for the whole curve.

The joint refit of a grouped fit

bnec_group fits each level of a factor separately, and a group-level term such as ogl() or (nec | site) pools the levels towards a common curve. Neither fits one model in which every level has its own curve parameters estimated together, which is what this route adds. That posterior supports a contrast between two levels conditional on everything they share, which differencing the independent posteriors of a bnec_group fit cannot.

Each level is fitted the equation its own model weights favour, which is the bayesnecgroupfit analogue of what best_crossed does for a hurdle fit: that function returns the best growth equation and the best survival equation separately, and the two blocks of one joint hurdle model then carry different equations. One brms model can carry a different functional form per level, because the mean is arbitrary arithmetic over data columns and parameters: each level's equation is multiplied by an indicator that is one on that level's rows and zero elsewhere, and the terms are summed.

Where every level favours the same equation the sum reduces to that equation with each parameter's ~ 1 replaced by ~ 0 + <group_var>, which is dummy coding of the factor onto the curve, and that is what is built. model forces one equation at every level, which is the same reduced form.

A group-level term cannot be added to a refit whose levels chose different equations, because the levels then share no parameter for it to be written on. Pass model to fit one equation everywhere, which is the form such a term applies to.

disp_by_level decides whether the family's dispersion parameter is also estimated per level. FALSE shares one dispersion across the levels, which is the model for a measurement error that is a property of the assay rather than of the level.

ecx, nsec, nec, ecnsec and exceedance on the returned object give one row per level, and autoplot draws one panel per level. ecx, nsec and exceedance return the data.frame a bayesnecgroupfit returns, and nec adds columns naming each level's equation and the type of its estimate. A bayesnecgroupfit has no ecnsec method; bayesnecjointfit describes the table ecnsec returns here. Each level is estimated on its own prediction grid, so the estimate for a level is read off that level's curve alone.

See also

bnec_hurdle, bnec_group, crossed_weights, best_crossed, bnec

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bayesnec)
data(nec_data)
nec_data$y[nec_data$x > 2.5] <- 0
nec_data$tank <- factor(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(nec_data)))
fit <- bnec_hurdle(y ~ crf(x, c("nec3param", "nec4param", "ecx4param")),
                   data = nec_data)
# the pair crossed_weights() favours, refitted as one model
fit_j <- bnec_joint(fit)
# the same pair with a group-level effect the factorisation cannot carry
fit_r <- bnec_joint(fit, formula = y ~ crf(x, "nec3param") + (nec | tank))

# a grouped fit, refitted as one model with a value per level
data(nec_data)
nec_data$site <- factor(rep(c("a", "b"), length.out = nrow(nec_data)))
fits <- bnec_group(y ~ crf(x, c("nec3param", "nec4param")),
                   data = nec_data, group_var = "site")
joint <- bnec_joint(fits)
} # }
